value.rationale: The third temporal moment has a direct dynamical meaning: it is exactly the threshold for ordinary square-root emergence of complete nonzero-velocity histories for Gaussian self-memory. When it diverges, the onset is provably smaller, with continuously varying fractional exponents and a sharp logarithmic marginal law at p=4. This fills a natural gap left by the finite-high-moment expansion in the motivating theory, supplies concrete reproducible asymptotic constants, and distinguishes physically relevant heavy-tail memories from short-range memory beyond what a linear threshold or mere branch-existence test reveals. The statement does not rest on a routine isolated parameter increment or unsupported claims of general dynamical stability.
